chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one who narrated it, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the distance is far for one of you and the house is distant from him, let him go up to his home, pray two rak'ahs, and send the salam to our graves, for that reaches us.' And you send salam upon the Imams (peace be upon them) from afar as you send it from near, except that it is not correct for you to say 'I came to visit you,' but rather you should say in its place: 'I intended with my heart to visit, since I was unable to attend your shrine, and I directed my salam to you, knowing that it reaches you. Peace be upon you, so intercede for me with your Lord, Glory and Might be upon Him, and supplicate with whatever you wish.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform distant visitation (Ziyarah) to the Imams when unable to travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the spiritual efficacy of distant *ziyarah*, emphasizing that the Imams' awareness transcends physical distance, a concept rooted in Shia theology regarding the *barzakh* state. It refines the liturgical etiquette by distinguishing between physical presence and spiritual intention, instructing the believer to declare 'I intended to visit' rather than 'I visited,' thereby acknowledging the limitation of the body while affirming the connectivity of the soul. This practice underscores the continuous intercessory role of the Imams, linking the supplicant's prayers directly to their spiritual presence.
